svg.aria-label: Cermet demo: an agent's git push is denied, the operator allows one sentence, the push carries, and every decision lands in the receipt log
svg.text: cermet — the loop (40s; a scripted replica — the words are what the shipped CLI prints)

g.text: # a fresh box — install once, one consent
Cermet needs administrator access once to:
• create the local broker's own service account
• create its credential vault (readable by the broker alone)
• install and start the background service
• create the isolated agent IPC endpoints
[cermet-setup] persistent Cermet files do not contain the plaintext key; full host-image disclosure may permit recover
[cermet-setup] update checks: daily against https://github.com/suarezc/cermet/releases, run as you and never by the daem
on. The notice is LOCAL and nothing installs itself; applying an update stays `sudo cermet update`. Off: cermet update -
[cermet-setup] next: cermet connect github (or vercel, stripe)
# hand it the token once — into the broker's vault, not the agent's env
Route this repository's `origin` through Cermet? (git remote set-url origin cermet::github/you/your-app) [Y/n]:
Your token is in Cermet's vault. The agent never sees it.
Wired: origin → cermet::github/you/your-app. Plain `git push` now goes through Cermet.
# your agent finishes a change and pushes — ordinary git, no token in its world, and no sentence admits this repo yet
Delta compression using up to 8 threads
remote: cermet: no standing authority for main on you/your-app (github.push denied by sentence authority: no rule matche
remote: cermet: authority is human-only — ask your operator to apply:
remote: cermet: to allow: cermet rules allow 'github.push where owner = "you" and name = "your-app"'
remote: cermet: this push touches 2 path(s)
error: failed to push some refs to 'cermet::github/you/your-app'
# one denied request, zero contact with GitHub — and the exact sentence
# that would widen it, addressed to you, not the model
# your call. paste the suggested sentence; your password — not the agent's — signs it
cermet rules allow 'github.push where owner = "you" and name = "your-app"'
allow github.push where owner = "you" and name = "your-app"
cermet: password required to authorize: add Cermet rule: allow github.push where owner = "you" and name = "your-app"
added rule #1: allow github.push where owner = "you" and name = "your-app"
# the agent retries. nothing about the agent changed — only your authority did
Delta compression using up to 8 threads
remote: cermet: carried main@9f8734c2ab11 to you/your-app (request req_d374a1b84c02e9f7)
# and none of it is a story — every decision is a row, the deny included
2026-08-18T17:42:31.104829557Z ALLOW github.push req_d374a1b84c02e9f7 — allowed by: allow github.push where owner = "yo
2026-08-18T17:40:02.882417203Z DENIED github.push req_b81c22e07f3a5d94: github.push denied by sentence authority: no ru
le matches this request — branch=main mirror_old_oid=e41f09a8c3d2b7f6015e4a9c8d23b761f0a5c48e name=your-app new_oid=9f87
# one more thing — your authority isn't app state. export it to a file in the repo
Only the managed block is authority input. Prose is guidance, never policy.
allow github.push where owner = "you" and name = "your-app"
# that's the loop: sentences as the only authority, a receipt for every decision —
# and the whole corpus is a file in your repo. commit it; a rebuilt box recovers it from git.
